page.layout: Top: two engraved medallion portraits side by side, each with a legend around its rim (left: PORTIA BRVTI VXOR; right: MARTIA.CAT FILIA). Below them: one column of running text with a four-line verse and a two-line verse set in italic, then a second paragraph. Below the text: an ornamental block with no printed text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: PORTIA Catonis Vticensis filia, vxórque Bruti fuit: hæc
accepta viri morte, cùm ipsa quoque mori statuisset, nec diu
superesse viro quem tantopere diligebat, nemo amicorum
assentiebatur: quinimo diligenti cura cùm id prohiberent, hæc
ex igne ardentes prunas corripiens, in os sibi coniecit, deinde
os, diémque clausit. Plutar. in vita Bruti. Vale. lib. 3. & 4. ca. 2.
& 6. Appi. lib. 15. De hac sic scribit Martialis, lib. Epigramma-

l.i: Coniugis audisset fatum cum Portia Bruti,
Et subtracta sibi quaereret arma dolor:
Nondum scitis (ait) mortem non posse negari:
Crederam satis hoc vos docuisse patrem.
Dixit, & ardentes avido bibit ore fauillas:
I nunc, & ferrum, turba molesta, nega.

main_text.l: MARTIA, Catonis filia minor fuit, quæ cùm interroga-

page.notes: The coin legends are printed inside the engravings and are given above as read; "MARTIA" has its initial M partly cut by the rim, and the legend is read from the scan. The verse is set as one paragraph per stanza, as the rules require, so the printed line breaks are not kept. The swash initial N of "Nondum" is copied as a plain N. Reading of "fauillas" and "Crederam" follows the scan; no doubtful words. Long s is written as s throughout, including "Eras." for the printed "Eraf.". The ornament below the text is a printed block with no words and is not transcribed.
